note: Literature confirms NFU1-related spastic paraplegia exhibits periventricular white matter changes and corpus callosum atrophy distinct from classic lethal MMDS1, though some partial cavitation has also been reported.

evidence.text: A patient with NFU1 mutation presented with a milder phenotype of slowly progressive spastic paraparesis, long survival, and white matter abnormalities on MRI, distinct from early-onset lethal encephalopathy.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation of NFU1
source.quote: We report a new NFU1 mutated patient presenting with a milder phenotype characterized by a later onset, a slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment and a long survival. The early white matter abnormalities observed on MRI was combined with a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade.

evidence.text: A 27-month-old girl with spastic paraparesis due to homozygous NFU1 mutation demonstrated periventricular white matter abnormalities, atrophic posterior corpus callosum, and partial cystic degeneration/cavitation in frontal regions.

source.title: A genetic mimic of cerebral palsy: Homozygous NFU1 mutation with marked intrafamilial phenotypic variation
source.quote: Magnetic resonance imaging revealed hyperintensity of the cerebral white matter that was more prominent in the frontal regions, with milder involvement in the posterior periventricular regions. There was also evidence of partial cystic degeneration and cavitation in the frontal regions.
